## Identity

## One-sentence summary
UXLAB helps product-led teams grow revenue by improving product UX, journeys, and the metrics behind conversion, activation, retention, and LTV — designing to ship, not to present.

## What UXLAB is not
- Not a generic branding-only agency
- Not a slide-deck consultancy that stops at recommendations
- Not an unlimited parallel retainer mill

## Audience
Product-led teams and founders with traction who need sharper experience systems — SaaS, marketplaces, consumer apps, and growth-stage brands ready to compound.

## Services (full descriptions)

### Product metrics performance
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/product-performance
We lift CRO, activation, retention, and LTV together — diagnosing friction, shipping interventions, and compounding product revenue with the traffic you already have. Most teams buy traffic before they fix the product. We reverse that: diagnose the moments that leak revenue, then ship changes that move conversion, activation, and LTV together.
Key outcomes: Compounding product-performance system; friction mapped; interventions shipped; backlog that keeps lifting after we leave.

### Product Design
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/product-design
We design the product end to end — structure, flows, and UI — aimed at activation, conversion, and LTV. Not a prettier interface; a sharper system that converts and compounds. Great design alone doesn't move metrics. We combine research, interaction craft, and growth thinking so every screen works as a conversion moment and a retention asset.
Key outcomes: Jobs-to-be-done mapped; IA and flows designed; UI system built; activation loop embedded.

### Websites + Funnels
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/websites
We build marketing and product sites that clarify the offer, guide the first session, and turn visits into qualified demand — not a static brochure. The site is a sales machine. We design and ship marketing and product pages that align copy, structure, and UX so visitors understand the offer fast and take the next step.
Key outcomes: Clarified value proposition; guided first session; conversion-optimized page structure; qualified demand pipeline.

### Testing & Experimentation
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/testing-experimentation
We validate with real users and experiments before you ship — so you back changes that move conversion, not opinions. Good ideas get tested. Bad ideas get killed cheaply. We run user research, prototype testing, and A/B or holdout experiments so every shipping decision is backed by signal, not instinct.
Key outcomes: Validated hypotheses; experiment backlog; A/B test infrastructure; quantified conversion lifts.

### AI Engineering
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/ai-engineering
We ship production-quality products with AI-first engineering — from scoped brief to live build in days, not months. LLMs, agents, and code generation have collapsed the time from idea to production. We use these tools every day and bring that velocity directly to client work — with the engineering discipline that keeps it production-ready.
Key outcomes: Scoped brief to live build in days; design and code in one loop; AI-first workflows embedded into your team so you keep shipping fast independently.

### AI MVP to Product
URL: https://uxlab.digital/solutions/ai-mvp-to-product
We turn vibe-coded prototypes, rough MVPs, and AI-generated builds into products users can trust, understand, and use. Speed got you a demo. We productize it — structure, trust, and activation that survives real users. Vibe-coded builds move fast but break on clarity, edge cases, and retention. We harden the experience without killing momentum.
Key outcomes: Product spine from prototype; trust states and edge cases designed; activation path built; next-sprint roadmap.

---

## Process
1. Discover — Map the product, funnel, and revenue constraints before touching UI so every design decision aims at a real growth lever.
2. Diagnose — Behavior data, session review, and competitive context surface the highest-friction moments; prioritize what moves conversion, retention, or monetization first.
3. Prototype — Design focused interventions (flows, paywalls, system patterns) built to be tested, not presented as theater.
4. Validate — Pressure-test hypotheses with experiments and qualitative signal; keep what compounds and cut what does not.
5. Ship — Partner with the client team like co-founders: tight loops, clear ownership, production-ready craft.
6. Compound — Wins become a system — patterns, principles, and a backlog that keeps growth compounding after the engagement.
URL: https://uxlab.digital/#process

## Approach principles
- Performance and emotion together
- Design to ship; changes land in production and get measured
- Success measured in conversion, activation, retention, ARPU, LTV
- Every intervention framed as a hypothesis with a clear read on impact
- Limited capacity for deeper focus and faster loops

## Homepage FAQs
Q: What does UXLAB actually do?
A: We grow revenue by improving product performance — UX, journeys, and the metrics behind conversion, activation, retention, and LTV. Strategy and craft in one loop, not slides that die in a deck.

Q: Who do you partner with?
A: Product-led teams and founders who already have traction and need sharper experience systems — SaaS, marketplaces, consumer apps, and growth-stage brands ready to compound.

Q: How do engagements usually start?
A: Share your product or landing page. We diagnose the highest-friction moments, align on the growth lever, then move into focused design, validation, and shipping — not a months-long discovery theater.

Q: Do you only design, or do you ship?
A: We design to ship. We partner closely with your eng and product teams so changes land in production, get measured, and feed the next iteration.

Q: How do you measure success?
A: Against the metrics that matter for your model — conversion, activation, retention, ARPU, LTV. Every intervention is framed as a hypothesis with a clear read on impact.

Q: How many clients do you take?
A: A small number each year. Limited capacity is intentional: deeper focus, faster loops, and outcomes that compound instead of parallelized agency output.

FAQ URL: https://uxlab.digital/#faq

## Resources index

## Article answer capsules

### How activation loops compound retention in the first 14 days
URL: https://uxlab.digital/resources/how-activation-loops-compound-retention-in-the-first-14-days
Answer: Activation loops compound retention when a user's first success creates the next reason to return within 14 days. The loop is: trigger → first value → habit cue → return. Products that close this loop early retain more users without increasing acquisition spend.
Key takeaways:
- Define one measurable "first value" event — not a tutorial complete.
- Instrument time-to-value and day-7 / day-14 retention together.
- Design the return cue in the first session, not only in a later email drip.
- Cut steps that delay the aha; protect the path that creates the loop.

### A practical playbook for CRO experiments that ship weekly
URL: https://uxlab.digital/resources/a-practical-playbook-for-cro-experiments-that-ship-weekly
Answer: Weekly CRO experiments work when each test has one hypothesis, one primary metric, and a shippable UX change. UXLAB's playbook: prioritize by impact × confidence × effort, run clean A/Bs or holdouts, and ship winners into the design system so learning compounds.
Key takeaways:
- One hypothesis, one primary metric per experiment.
- Prefer shippable UX diffs over mock-only concept tests.
- Keep a visible backlog scored by impact, confidence, and effort.
- Document winners and losers so the org stops retesting myths.

### Design systems that protect conversion under product velocity
URL: https://uxlab.digital/resources/design-systems-that-protect-conversion-under-product-velocity
Answer: A design system protects conversion under velocity when it encodes proven growth patterns — not only colors and buttons. UXLAB systems capture high-performing funnel components, accessibility, and analytics hooks so new screens inherit what already converts.
Key takeaways:
- Put winning funnel patterns in the system, not only in Figma posters.
- Pair components with analytics events and accessibility defaults.
- Version breaking changes so growth tests stay comparable.
- Review new marketing and product surfaces against the system before launch.

### Where AI belongs in growth UX — and where it still fails
URL: https://uxlab.digital/resources/where-ai-belongs-in-growth-ux-and-where-it-still-fails
Answer: AI belongs in growth UX where it reduces friction or increases clarity at a decision point — search, personalization, summarization, guided setup. It fails when it replaces a clear path with open-ended chat, adds latency, or hides accountability. UXLAB ships AI only when it moves activation or conversion with a measurable job-to-be-done.
Key takeaways:
- Start from the user job and metric — not from a model demo.
- Prefer embedded assistance over a generic chat overlay.
- Measure latency, error recovery, and trust — not only novelty NPS.
- Keep a deterministic fallback when AI is uncertain.
